claims.text: Conventional EAM references cannot adequately represent the variety of local atomic configurations in ab initio high-temperature liquids.
This EAM underrepresentation leads to sizable thermodynamic-integration path mismatches.
An MLIP trained on diverse ab initio liquid configurations will represent liquid local bonding environments more accurately than a conventional EAM reference.
Including high-temperature solid configurations in the training set will make the MLIP suitable as a reference for high-temperature solid states as well as liquids.
The high-dimensional fitting capability of an MLIP can encapsulate the many local atomic arrangements found in an ab initio high-temperature liquid.
More accurate representation of local environments and fluctuations will improve mapping between the disordered ab initio target and its reference state.
A liquid-trained MLIP will reproduce the ab initio energy landscape more faithfully than an EAM reference.
More faithful reproduction of the ab initio energy landscape will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Replacing TOR-TILD's EAM reference with the proposed MLIP will significantly reduce TI path-mismatch error.
The reduction in TI path-mismatch error could exceed 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reducing TI path mismatch with an MLIP reference will produce more accurate free-energy differences.
The intervention applies to nearly equiatomic, chemically complex high-entropy alloys at approximately 0.9Tm to Tm.
The expected improvement applies to high-entropy alloys having modest atomic-size differences and high configurational complexity near their melting temperatures.
The effectiveness of the intervention may not extend to systems with extreme atomic-size mismatches or temperatures significantly removed from Tm.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on the quality and breadth of the ab initio training data and on the alloy system.
